title: binary16 addition under roundNearestTiesToEven is monotone in its first argument
statement: Let F be the IEEE-754 binary16 interchange format, SMT-LIB `(_ FloatingPoint 5 11)`, and let RNE denote roundNearestTiesToEven. For all values a, b, c of F: if fp.leq(a, b) holds and neither fp.add(RNE, a, c) nor fp.add(RNE, b, c) is NaN, then fp.leq(fp.add(RNE, a, c), fp.add(RNE, b, c)). This is the binary16 instance of F:fp8-add-monotone-rne, and it is recorded `open` because AXEYUM HAS NOT SETTLED IT -- not because it is doubted.

formal.statement: (assert (=> (and (fp.leq a b) (not (fp.isNaN (fp.add RNE a c))) (not (fp.isNaN (fp.add RNE b c)))) (fp.leq (fp.add RNE a c) (fp.add RNE b c))))

provenance.established_by: not established here. Recorded by the fp-kernels lane as a reachable target with a measured baseline.
provenance.source: authored here as the binary16 instance of F:fp8-add-monotone-rne, which IS settled, by exhaustive enumeration at 8 bits.

prior_art.what: That each rounding-direction attribute defines a monotone map from the extended reals to the format, so a correctly-rounded operation inherits the monotonicity of the exact operation it rounds -- which gives the statement for every format, this one included.
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source, and records the citation as the received one.

prior_art.what: Both report `unsat` on the negation, i.e. both prove the statement, in 30.6s and 8.3s respectively on artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-fp16-add-monotone-rne.smt2 (measured 2026-08-14, same machine, release builds).
prior_art.where: run locally by the fp-kernels lane; the file is in this repository
prior_art.attribution: measured by this lane, not cited. Recorded under prior_art because these are OTHER systems establishing the fact -- deliberately NOT recorded as `evidence`, since evidence rows here would make the ledger say axeyum established something it did not.

notes:
WHY THIS FACT IS `open` AND ITS 8-BIT SIBLING IS `proved`. F:fp8-add-monotone-rne is settled by enumerating all 2^24 fp8 E5M2 triples in about three seconds. The identical proposition at binary16 is 2^48 triples, so brute force is gone, and the symbolic route is where axeyum currently cannot follow: the fp8 version of this query -- three free symbols and four fp.add circuits -- ran 50 minutes in a release build without deciding, and binary16 is strictly larger. bitwuzla settles the binary16 file in 8.3 seconds.

SO THIS IS A MEASURED PARITY GAP, WRITTEN DOWN AS A TARGET. `epistemic_status` is a statement about THIS ledger, and the honest value is `open`: we have not established it. `external_status` is `proved` because two independent solvers have. The evidence array is empty on purpose -- a filled one would read as axeyum having done the work.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT. Nothing about the mathematics; the statement follows from monotonicity of correct rounding. The gap is entirely in the FP-to-bit-vector route's throughput on a multi-operand comparison miter. `artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-fp16-add-monotone-rne.smt2` is the reproducible target, byte-identical to the file the two oracles were timed on.

ARITY IS THE WALL, NOT WIDTH. F:fp32-doubling-add-equals-mul-two is a UNARY claim at binary32 and was enumerated over all 2^32 inputs in 51 seconds. Ternary claims lose brute force at 8 bits already. That is why this fact and its 8-bit sibling exist as a pair.

MEASURED AGAIN 2026-08-22, AND THE DECISION HALF OF THIS NOTE IS NOW WRONG.
`axeyum_cli` decides this file `unsat` in **11.5 s, reproducibly** — faster than
z3's 30.6 s on the same machine and within 1.4x of bitwuzla's 8.3 s. The claim
above that "the symbolic route is where axeyum currently cannot follow" described
the state on 2026-08-14 and no longer holds; the 50-minute non-decision it cites
was the fp8 SYMBOLIC route before subsequent solver work.

WHAT HAS NOT CLOSED IS THE CERTIFICATE, and that is why this fact is still
`open`. Run through `smtcomp_cli --evidence`, which produces and re-checks a DRAT
refutation rather than merely deciding, the same query exceeded **183 minutes**
at 99.8% CPU with resident memory flat at 0.34 GB — working, not thrashing. For
calibration the fp8 sibling, a strictly smaller problem, took 25m46s with
evidence.

So the honest split is: **deciding costs 11.5 s, certifying costs more than three
hours and has not been observed to terminate.** That ratio is the finding. This
fact stays `open` because `epistemic_status` is a statement about what THIS
ledger can show, and a bare verdict with no checkable artifact is not evidence —
exactly the standard the rest of the ledger is held to.

CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-08-22, LATER THE SAME DAY: THE SIX HOURS WERE THE CHECKER,
NOT THE SOLVER. Progress instrumentation landed in `proof_sat.rs` and the first
bounded run answered it immediately:

    search   424,601 conflicts in 24.2 s -> 827,048 proof steps, 193 MB
    then     progress stops -- the search has RETURNED, at a genuine terminal
             state, not the deadline and not the conflict cap
    then     the remaining time is `check_drat` + `elaborate_drat_to_lrat`,
             which have no deadline and no observability of their own

So certificate PRODUCTION is fast; certificate CHECKING and LRAT elaboration over
a 193 MB proof is what does not terminate. The fp8 sibling confirms the shape:
1.3 s of search, 8.9 MB of proof, and roughly 25 minutes of check+elaborate. At
21.7x the proof size, fp16's check stage is the wall.

The earlier note in this file extrapolated 822 years from the search-space ratio.
That number measured the wrong stage and should be read as void: search scales
about 18x here for a 2^24-fold larger space, which is fine. What scales badly is
elaboration in proof size.

This fact remains `open` for the same reason as before -- no checkable artifact --
but the target has moved. It is not "make the solver faster"; it is "make a
193 MB refutation checkable", which is what cube-and-conquer (ADR-0543) addresses
by producing many small per-cube proofs instead of one large one.

RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28, decidable-frontier lane. This is a confirming re-run, not a new finding, and epistemic_status stays `open` -- nothing here is a checkable artifact.

DECIDE-ONLY, reconfirmed: `axeyum_cli` on artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-fp16-add-monotone-rne.smt2 -> `unsat` in 11.09 s wall (release build, host load ~1.7-1.8/16). Matches the 11.5 s figure from 2026-08-22 within noise -- the decision route has not regressed or improved materially.

EVIDENCE/SEARCH, reconfirmed twice: `smtcomp_cli --evidence --progress` with an internal `--timeout-ms` watchdog. Both runs (120 s and 300 s budgets) show the identical search terminal state already recorded: 424,601 conflicts in 24.4-27.5 s (run-to-run variance) -> 827,048 proof steps, 193,214,020 bytes (~193 MB). Neither run produced a certified verdict inside its budget -- both printed `unknown`, exactly as expected for a watchdog firing mid-check.

CHECKING STAGE, now measured directly rather than inferred. The 120 s and 300 s runs (default `AXEYUM_CHECK_PROGRESS_INTERVAL=50000`) produced ZERO `; checking` lines -- i.e. `check_drat` had not reached even its first 50,000-step checkpoint after ~95 s and ~272 s of checking time respectively. Lowering the interval to `AXEYUM_CHECK_PROGRESS_INTERVAL=1000` on a fresh 90 s-budget run got five real `stage=drat_check` samples:

    steps=1000 elapsed_ms=9850  steps_per_sec=101.5
    steps=2000 elapsed_ms=25913 steps_per_sec=77.2
    steps=3000 elapsed_ms=27248 steps_per_sec=110.1
    steps=4000 elapsed_ms=46694 steps_per_sec=85.7
    steps=5000 elapsed_ms=49165 steps_per_sec=101.7

Average ~95 steps/s against a `total=827048`. Extrapolating at that measured rate: `drat_check` ALONE needs on the order of 8,700 s (~2.4 h) to finish re-deriving the refutation, before `elaborate_drat_to_lrat` (the second sub-stage, not reached in any run here) even starts. That is a real per-run measurement of the bottleneck this fact already named, not a repeat of the earlier extrapolation-from-a-different-stage error the 2026-08-22 note corrects -- `stage=drat_check` is explicit in every sampled line, so there is no ambiguity about which sub-stage is slow.

CONCLUSION UNCHANGED, now on firmer ground: deciding this query costs ~11 s; producing a checkable certificate costs multiple hours and was not observed to complete in any bounded run attempted here (up to 300 s of checking time, three separate invocations). The fact stays `open`. Nothing in `crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/` or `scripts/` was touched to get these numbers -- they come from the existing `smtcomp_cli --evidence --progress` instrumentation and `AXEYUM_CHECK_PROGRESS_INTERVAL`, run against the fact's own pinned negation file.

OBSTRUCTION LIFTED 2026-08-28, drat-evidence-route lane. THE CHECKING STAGE NOW COMPLETES. The note immediately above says certifying this query "costs multiple hours and was not observed to complete in any bounded run". That was true of the route that existed when it was written and is NO LONGER TRUE, so read it as history.

WHAT CHANGED (ADR-0613). The evidence path called `check_drat`, the FORWARD reference checker, at every accepting site -- not for a documented reason but because those call sites date from 2026-06-13 and the backward core-first engine (ADR-0382, ~66x) only landed 2026-08-12, additively, with its item 9 deferring exactly this follow-on. Nothing pinned the choice. `certify_unsat_via_lrat` now runs the backward engine as an UNTRUSTED producer of antecedent hints and has `check_lrat` -- small, search-free, linear -- verify those hints against the formula. The trusted base does not move: a `Certified` is discharged by `check_lrat` alone, and `check_drat_backward` appears only in rejecting position.

MEASURED, same pinned file, `smtcomp_cli --evidence --progress` (release, contended host, load ~9.4):

    search    424,601 conflicts in 27.748 s -> 827,048 proof steps, 193,214,020 bytes
    checking  stage=backward_lrat_certify  82.302 s  10,048.8 steps/sec  certified=true
    evidence  kind=unsat-drat certified=1 recheck=ok arena=ok ms=125098
    unsat

So: 125.098 s END TO END for a certified refutation, of which 82.3 s is checking. Against the 2026-08-28 measurement in the note above -- ~95 steps/sec, ~8,700 s extrapolated for `drat_check` ALONE before `elaborate_drat_to_lrat` even started -- that is roughly 106x on the checking stage. The binary8 sibling moved from a recorded 25m46s to 5.028 s on the same route.

THIS FACT IS STILL RECORDED `open`, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. `epistemic_status` is a statement about what this ledger can SHOW, and showing it requires an `evidence` row whose `checker_command` fails when the claim is false. That command does not exist yet: it needs a release build of `smtcomp_cli`, a discriminating exit status (the run prints `unsat` and `certified=1`; an exit status that depends only on the process completing would be exactly the checker-that-cannot-fail defect this repository audits for), and a verified negative control. The lane that measured this was scoped to notes on this file and did not write that row. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED is that the obstruction this fact was blocked on is gone; what is NOT established is the ledger evidence. Those are different claims and only the first is made here.
